newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds registered their sharpest fall in about three months after U.S. economic data sparked a dive in U.S. Treasuries.
The small gains shown by guilder paper evaporated as prices were marked down although cash activity was subdued.

The shorter end of the yield curve was the focus of most interest with buying reported for maturities between 1999 and 2002. "It started off quite tame today. We have seen more turnover in the afternoon," said one dealer.
The spark was the release of the Philadelphia business activity index, which rose to 25.2 in June from 1.6 in May.
One dealer said the news sent German bund futures diving.
"It's been a pretty quiet day but what we have done, we've done in Bunds," he said.
He noted some buying demand for 1999-2000 paper, attributing this hesitancy about buying longer bonds because of uncertainty over European economic and monetary union (EMU.)
The dealer said the outlook for Dutch bonds was slightly more negative than the previous day.
Another trader said the spread to Bunds and the shape of the yield curve changed little through the day as guilder paper tracked the movement in Germany.
He said 2000 and 2001 paper was fairly well bid.
Market players have been executing extension trades, swapping out of 1998 bonds.
